items.why: The report says "The ~352 cm-1 band is an unresolved doublet of 2LA(M) and E2g1", fits two Lorentzians and gets "2LA(M) 351.12" and "E2g1 355.30" for spot 1.

Spot 1 matches ("2LA(M)/A1g fitted height ratio ~2.35"), but for spot 2 the report gives only an area ratio of "≈ 0.9", not about 0.5, and the summary confusingly says 2LA(M) is "strongly enhanced at spot 2".
The report states "A1g is 417.28 cm-1 at spot 1 and 420.08 cm-1 at spot 2 (+2.8 cm-1 stiffening)", matching the 1L and bulk reference values.
The report gives "Δ = 61.98 cm-1" for spot 1 and "Δ = 64.70 cm-1" for spot 2, computed after the doublet was fitted as two components.
The report notes "3L and bulk cannot be separated by Δ (64.6 vs 64.8)", cites a 1L-2L gap of only 1.4 cm-1 and A1g reference steps of about 1 cm-1, and assigns spot 2 only as "≥3L".
The report checks calibration against the Si line ("Si offsets +0.21 and +0.09 cm-1 differ by only 0.12 cm-1") and says the 514.5 nm resonance controls the 2LA(M) intensity.

wrong_claims.why: The report rejects the single-peak approach explicitly: "Using the merged ~351.7/353.1 cm-1 peak as E2g gives Δ = 65.6 ... That is wrong for spot 1".
The report treats 2LA(M) as a resonant second-order mode, and it says LA(M) "is not a defect marker".
